{{Short description|Canadian mathematician}}
'''Michael Makkai''' ({{langx|hu|Makkai Mihály}}; 24 June 1939 in [[Budapest]], [[Kingdom of Hungary|Hungary]]) is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] of [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] origin, specializing in [[mathematical logic]].<ref name="BenthemHeinzmann2006">{{cite book|last1=Benthem|first1=Johan Van|last2=Heinzmann|first2=Gerhard|last3=Rebuschi|first3=Manuel|author4=Henk Visser|title=The age of alternative logics: assessing philosophy of logic and mathematics today|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5ycgFGs_0iYC&pg=PA182|accessdate=28 June 2011|date=2006-11-14|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-1-4020-5011-4|pages=182–}}</ref> He works in [[model theory]], [[category theory]], [[algebraic logic]], [[type theory]] and the theory of [[topos|topoi]]. 

== Career ==
=== Academic biography ===
Makkai was awarded his PhD from the [[Eötvös Loránd University]], Budapest, in 1966, having been supervised by [[Rózsa Péter]] and [[Andrzej Mostowski]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=62420}}</ref> 
He then worked at the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|Mathematical Institute]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Makkai's CV at his McGill University Homepage|url=http://www.math.mcgill.ca/makkai/Various/CV0001.pdf}}</ref> 
Between 1974 and 2010, he was professor of mathematics at [[McGill University]], retiring in 2010. 
He is also an external member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (1995).

=== Work ===
With [[Leo Harrington]] and [[Saharon Shelah]] he proved the [[Vaught conjecture]] for ω-stable theories.<ref>[[Leo Harrington|L. Harrington]], M. Makkai, [[Saharon Shelah|S. Shelah]]: A proof of Vaught's conjecture for ω-stable theories, ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]'',  '''49'''(1984), 259&ndash;280.</ref>

With Robert Paré he further developed the theory of [[Accessible category|Accessible Categories]].<ref>M. Makkai, R. Paré: ''Accessible categories: the foundations of categorical model theory''. Contemporary Mathematics, '''104'''. American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 1989. viii+176 pp.&nbsp;{{ISBN|0-8218-5111-X}}, {{doi|10.1090/conm/104}}</ref>

Makkai has an [[Erdős number]] of 1, having published "Some Remarks on Set Theory, X" with [[Paul Erdős]] in 1966.<ref>Paul Erdős, Michael Makkai: Some Remarks on Set Theory, X, Stud. Sci. Math. Hungar. 1, 157-159 (1966)</ref>
